name: Biology
description: Cell and molecular biology, genetics, physiology, ecology and evolution.

figureTypes.name: 3D structure
figureTypes.description: Proteins and nucleic acids from Protein Data Bank (PDB) files, or schematic models built from cited dimensions.

figureTypes.name: Cell schematic
figureTypes.description: Labeled schematic of a cell or organelle, with a scale bar or a 'not to scale' note.

figureTypes.name: Pathway diagram
figureTypes.description: Metabolic, signaling or gene-regulation pathways as labeled boxes and arrows.

figureTypes.name: Plot from equations or data
figureTypes.description: Growth curves, scaling laws, population models from cited data.

conventions: Use SI prefixes for size: nanometres (nm) for molecules, micrometres (µm) for cells; state which at first use.
Write gene names in italics and protein names in roman type.
Give DNA length in base pairs (bp), kilobases (kb) or megabases (Mb) and say which.

safetyNotes: This book explains biology; it is not a laboratory protocol. Work with living organisms, tissues or DNA only under the biosafety rules of a supervised laboratory.
restrictedDetail: Methods to culture, enhance, modify or spread pathogens or toxins
Step-by-step protocols for producing biological agents
draftingNotes: Distinguish what is well established from what is current research, and say which.
When a 3D structure is schematic (built from average dimensions rather than a PDB entry), say so in the caption.
